title: Fukushima Daiichi 2011 — measured Cs-137 ground deposition against the plume model
publisher: Japanese government (MEXT, later NRA) aerial radiation monitoring; compiled by IRSN (France)
src: Dumont Le Brazidec J., Saunier O. (2022) Statistics on caesium 137 deposition around the Fukushima-Daiichi plant after the 2011 accident. Zenodo. doi:10.5281/zenodo.7016491 — aerial monitoring results of MEXT/NRA, cell means compiled by IRSN — CC BY 4.0
credit: Dumont Le Brazidec & Saunier (2022), IRSN — Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.7016491, CC BY 4.0; underlying measurements: MEXT / Nuclear Regulation Authority, Japan. Wind: ERA5 (Hersbach et al. 2020, Copernicus Climate Change Service) via Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0.
paidBy: Fukushima Cs-137 deposition survey (MEXT/NRA via IRSN, CC BY 4.0)
asOfNote: The IRSN file does not state its reference date. The paper that uses it (Dumont Le Brazidec et al. 2023, GMD 16:1039) cites MEXT/NRA, "Results of the Fifth Airborne Monitoring Survey and Airborne Monitoring Survey Outside 80 km", 28 Sep 2012, whose Cs-137 maps are decay-compensated to 2012-06-28. That is the date used; at Cs-137's 30.08-year half-life a different compensation date within 2011-2012 moves the values by under 4%.

conditions.wind: ERA5 reanalysis via Open-Meteo archive, 10 m and 100 m, nests = RAD.innerPlan / RAD.outerPlan

release.credit: Katata G., Chino M., Kobayashi T., Terada H., Ota M., Nagai H., Kajino M., Draxler R., Hort M. C., Malo A., Torii T., Sanada Y. (2015) Atmos. Chem. Phys. 15, 1029–1070, doi:10.5194/acp-15-1029-2015 — Japan Atomic Energy Agency, CC BY 3.0.
release.paidBy: Fukushima Daiichi release time series (JAEA, Katata et al. 2015, CC BY 3.0)
release.inferred: Release rates were estimated by reverse modelling (WSPEEDI-II against measured air concentrations and dose rates); the paper reports that the result reproduces the airborne deposition surveys. Agreement of another model with the survey under this release is therefore not an independent test.
